request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A person can now have several holds, each with a from-date and an optional to-date. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How totals work now**
- An open claim is left out of the live totals only if it is dated within one of the person's holds (both dates count as inside) and no statement binds it. "Open" includes pending claims, as it did before.
- Settled claims always count, and so do claims bound by a statement, whatever their date.
- This one rule is used everywhere totals are worked out: on the server (rollup, statement, closing a period) and on screen (claimed, due-total, overdue, the rollup line, periods, summary, export, patrons).
- "On hold" shows yes if the person has any hold at all, even one that has already ended.

**Storage**
- A new migration, `V30__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table and drops the old `held` column.
- Anyone who was held before is given one hold with no end date, starting from `0001-01-01`, so their totals don't change.

**Server**
- The hold endpoint now takes `{from, to}`. A blank from-date means the sheet's today, and a blank to-date means the hold never ends.
- A badly formed date, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused with the usual person error and nothing is saved.
- Holding writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=… from=<date>`, followed by the rollup lines as before.
- Releasing is gone: `TogglePersonHold` is replaced by `HoldPerson`, and `PERSON_RELEASED` is no longer written.

**Screen**
- Each person row has from-date and to-date inputs and a "Hold" button that adds a hold.
- The row lists each hold on its own line, such as "2026-03-05 to 2026-03-08", or "to open" when there is no end date.
- There is no "Release" button any more.

Two choices go beyond what the request spelled out:
- A pending claim that a statement covers is not treated as bound, because it shows its live figure. So it is left out of the totals if it falls within a hold.
- A to-date before the from-date is refused rather than saved.
